Subject: Phased snapshot preservation and rolling deletion windows - order form Q&A

Hi Ben,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form (attached). Our legal and ops teams reviewed and have a few questions specifically around how Redwood handles post-retention snapshots and staggered deletion windows. High-level asks:  

- Can Redwood preserve immutable snapshots for up to 45 days after the primary retention window expires to support e-discovery requests? We want a documented process we can invoke (not ad-hoc).
- Is it possible to have a phased deletion schedule on the order form: e.g., after retention end (T0) move data to a cold snapshot tier for 30 days (T0–T30), then a deeper archive for an additional 60 days (T30–T90), and finally certified deletion at T90?
- For the snapshot preservation, we need an option to replicate the snapshot to a separate geography (EU vs US) with separate KMS keys for additional resiliency — is that supported and how is it billed?
- We also need a deletion certification process: a signed attestation and a machine-readable report listing object IDs removed.

Attached: DataCare_OrderForm_v3.pdf — we’ve annotated sections 3.2 and 7.

Can you confirm whether the order form can include explicit exhibit language for the phased windows and the certification workflow? If so, please send proposed wording we can redline.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of InfoSec, DataCare Systems

Subject: Re: Phased snapshot preservation and rolling deletion windows - order form Q&A

Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated order form. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a documented 'phased snapshot preservation' flow and provide deletion certifications; geo-replication with separate KMS is also supported as an add-on. Details below and I’ve looped in Marissa (CS) and Karthik (Contracts/Sales-Eng) for the contractual language and cost impacts.

Technical/operational summary:
- Phased windows: We can model the timeline you outlined as discrete lifecycle phases (Hot -> Cold snapshot -> Deep Archive -> Purge). Each phase transition is governed by the order form exhibit A (Lifecycle Exhibit).
- Snapshot preservation: We offer a snapshot hold feature that pins a read-only snapshot and prevents garbage collection for up to 60 days if elected (default 30 days). We can set to 45 days per your request; we’ll capture this as a configurable field in the order form.
- Geo-replication & KMS separation: Supported. Replication to an alternate region (e.g., eu-west-1) will incur storage + egress delta pricing and a separate KMS key is required if you want customer-managed keys.
- Deletion certification: We can produce a signed attestation + a CSV report of object IDs and timestamps. For higher assurance, we can also provide cryptographic proof (SHA256 digest) per object.

Operational notes and caveats:
- Emergency legal hold: we can support a legal-hold API to suspend automated purges, but there is a 72-hour lead time for enforced snapshot pin-roll (to allow in-flight jobs to quiesce). If you need near-instant holds, that should be scoped as a premium SLA.
- Cost: snapshot preservation will be charged at the cold-tier snapshot rate; geo-replication billed separately. We’ll provide a simple cost table to add to the order form.

I’m attaching a very small lifecycle diagram Marissa created to illustrate the phase transitions. Marissa — can you propose suggested wording for Exhibit A (lifecycle windows + certification process)? Karthik — any concerns we should flag for the contract team?

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — adding a couple operational specifics so you have concrete language to consider for Exhibit A:  

- Lifecycle phases (example wording):
  • Phase 1 — Hot retention: data accessible for normal inference and subject to primary retention per Section 3.1.
  • Phase 2 — Snapshot preservation (T0–T30/45/60): pinned snapshots retained in read-only storage; not subject to automatic token trimming or KV purge. Customer may request snapshot export during this window.
  • Phase 3 — Deep archive (T30/45–T90): compressed, encrypted archive stored in cold tier; retrieval within 72 hours.
  • Phase 4 — Certified deletion (T90): permanent deletion triggered; Redwood will provide deletion certification within 5 business days.

- Geo-replication details: we can replicate the snapshot to a separate region and optionally encrypt with a customer-managed key (CMK). If you require cross-border replication (US->EU), we will include a data processing addendum reflecting additional transfer controls.

- Auditability: we keep immutable audit logs of lifecycle transitions for 1 year by default; extended log retention can be purchased. The deletion certificate will include object IDs, deletion timestamp, and the name of the actor who executed the purge.

Ben, Karh tik — suggested Exhibit A wording attached in plain text; happy to convert to a redline for the order form.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Elena / Ben — quick contract-level note from our side. We can accept Exhibit A as described, subject to the following committed language:  

1) Snapshot Preservation Addendum: Redwood will retain pinned snapshots for up to 60 days from T0 if the customer selects the Snapshot Preservation Addendum in the Order Form. Customer may elect a custom retention less than or equal to 60 days at signature.

2) Emergency Legal Hold: Redwood will implement a legal hold suspension within 72 hours of notice unless the customer purchases the expedited hold SLA. During a legal hold, scheduled automated purges are suspended; charges for continued snapshot storage apply.

3) Deletion Certification: Redwood will provide a deletion attestation (signed PDF) and a machine-readable CSV of deleted object IDs within 5 business days of the final purge window. For customers requiring cryptographic proofs, Redwood will include SHA256 digests as an optional line item.

4) Audit Logs & Evidence: Redwood retains lifecycle and purge audit logs for 12 months by default. Extended retention and offsite escrow of logs can be added as Exhibit B.

5) Pricing: Geo-replication with CMK is billed as incremental storage + egress + key-management fee; we will provide precise numbers in the pricing table.

If these points are acceptable, please confirm and we will produce a clean Order Form (Exhibit A + pricing table + Exhibit B outline) for redline/signature. CC'ing DataCare Legal for visibility.

— Karthik
